## Problem
Feature to add: Data saving: a DataService on the server saves each player's Cash, TotalEarned, Rebirths and owned upgrade ids with DataStoreService (store 'CubeCashTycoon_v1', key 'p_<UserId>'), loading on join before their Tycoon starts (re-applying owned upgrades), autosaving every 60 seconds, on PlayerRemoving and in game:BindToClose. Every DataStore call is wrapped in pcall with a couple of retries; when DataStore is unavailable (Studio without API access, or any error) it falls back to an in-memory table so the game still runs with no errors or warnings in the output (one quiet print, never warn). Bump counters data_loaded and data_saved.
Change needed in this file: Add two small functions. getOwnedIds(player) returns an array of the upgrade ids the player owns. restoreOwned(player, ids) marks those ids as owned without charging or bumping 'upgrades_bought'. It re-applies their effects (dropper count, speed, multipliers, pad visibility) immediately if the player's plot is already claimed. If not, it stores the ids as pending and applies them when the plot is claimed. Ignore unknown ids, and ids whose 'requires' prerequisite is missing from the owned set.
New feature files: ServerScriptService/DataService.luau. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: data_loaded, data_saved.

## Context
Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code

-- keeps only known ids whose 'requires' prerequisite is also in the valid set
local function validateIds(ids: any): { string }
	local want: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	if type(ids) == "table" then
		for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
			if type(id) == "string" and byId[id] then
				want[id] = true
			end
		end
	end
	local ok: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	local changed = true
	while changed do
		changed = false
		for id in pairs(want) do
			if not ok[id] then
				local req = byId[id].requires
				if req == nil or ok[req] then
					ok[id] = true
					changed = true
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local out = {}
	for id in pairs(ok) do
		table.insert(out, id)
	end
	return out
end

local function applyOwned(state: any, ids: { string })
	for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
		state.owned[id] = true
	end
	local mods = computeMods(state.owned)
	if type(Tycoon.setModifiers) == "function" then
		Tycoon.setModifiers(state.player, mods)
	end
	refresh(state)
	sendOwned(state.player)
end

-- array of upgrade ids the player currently owns
function UpgradeService.getOwnedIds(player: Player): { string }
	local ids = {}
	local state = states[player]
	if state then
		for id, v in pairs(state.owned) do
			if v then
				table.insert(ids, id)
			end
		end
	else
		local pending = pendingOwned[player]
		if pending then
			for _, id in ipairs(pending) do
				table.insert(ids, id)
			end
		end
	end
	return ids
end

-- marks saved upgrades as owned (no charge, no telemetry); applies now or when the plot is claimed
function UpgradeService.restoreOwned(player: Player, ids: any)
	local valid = validateIds(ids)
	local state = states[player]
	if state and plots[player] then
		pendingOwned[player] = nil
		applyOwned(state, valid)
	else
		pendingOwned[player] = valid
	end
